reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be an arbitrary finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its compatible norm and Borel measurable structure. Write gamma_E for the measure defined by stdGaussian E. Concretely, if (e_k) is the standard orthonormal basis used in the definition, gamma_E is the pushforward of the finite product of real Gaussian laws gaussianReal(0,1) by (z_k) -> sum_k z_k e_k. The supplied density fixes each coordinate law as (2*pi)^(-1/2) exp(-t^2/2) dt: the mean is zero and the variance is one. Thus the Gaussian normalization is specified, not an unspecified scale. All integrals below are real Bochner/Lebesgue integrals over the whole E with respect to this same gamma_E.

Let u and v be any vectors in E with ||u||=1 and ||v||=1, and let i,j be arbitrary natural numbers, including zero. Define polynomials H_m in Z[X] by the supplied recurrence
 H_0(X)=1,
 H_(m+1)(X)=X H_m(X)-H_m'(X).
In real-valued formulas H_m(t) means evaluation at t after mapping each integer coefficient into R. This is exactly Polynomial.aeval t (Polynomial.hermite m). The recurrence gives H_1(t)=t and H_2(t)=t^2-1 and fixes the normalization; no factorial or square-root-factorial normalization is applied to H_m itself.

Define the actual real function on E
 G(x)=H_i(<u,x>) H_j(<v,x>).
Then G is integrable with respect to gamma_E and
 integral_E G(x) d gamma_E(x)
   = { i! * <u,v>^i, if i=j;
       0,             if i!=j. }

The factorial i! is a natural number cast to R, and the power is the ordinary real base <u,v> raised to the natural exponent i. It is not |<u,v>|^i, so the sign for negative overlap and odd i is retained. The zero-degree case uses 0!=1 and a^0=1, including a=0. The measure is the same standard Gaussian for both factors, so this is a shared-x mixed moment; no independence, orthogonality, or linear independence of u and v is assumed. The only vector restrictions are their two unit-norm conditions. There is no additional lower bound on dim E, although in dimension zero unit vectors do not exist. Integrability of G is part of the conclusion rather than a premise. The theorem does not separately assert that either factor belongs to L2, an orthonormal-basis completeness result, or a joint-law construction. There is no time parameter, horizon, limiting sense or existential constant.
objects: A finite-dimensional real inner-product space E with its Borel structure and standard Gaussian gamma_E; unit vectors u,v; natural indices i,j; integer-coefficient polynomials H_m determined by H_0=1 and H_(m+1)=XH_m-H_m prime; G(x)=H_i(<u,x>)H_j(<v,x>) with integer coefficients evaluated in R.
domains: u,v,x lie in E. i,j range over all Nat including zero. H_m lies in Z[X]; its aeval at a real inner product is real. G:E->R and its integral are real. Both factors use the same x integrated against gamma_E. No independent sample or measure is introduced.
quantifiers: For every E with the specified real inner-product, finite-dimensional, norm and Borel structures, every u,v:E satisfying ||u||=1 and ||v||=1, and every i,j:Nat, define G by the displayed product and conclude both its integrability and the conditional integral formula. G is locally defined, not an additional arbitrary function or existential witness.
assumptions: Only the carrier structures and the two unit-norm equations. No positive degree, positive dimension, independence, orthogonality, distinctness of directions, positivity of overlap or pre-assumed integrability.
conclusion: Integrable_gamma_E G and integral_gamma_E G = if i=j then (i! cast to R)*<u,v>^i else 0. The factorial is i factorial and the overlap is raised to i in the equality branch.
scopes: The polynomial functions are literal everywhere-defined functions. Integrability is a conclusion over all E, and the second conclusion is an exact real mixed-moment identity. There is no a.e. assertion about G values, no quotient-representative choice, no time/horizon and no limit. The zero-degree, equal/opposite-direction and negative-overlap cases are included as typed.
constant_dependencies: No unspecified or existential constants. Gaussian coordinates have mean zero and variance one. Hermite normalization is fixed by H_(m+1)=XH_m-H_m prime with H_0=1, giving the factor i! and raw overlap power <u,v>^i. There is no 2^i factor, no normalized polynomial by sqrt(i!), no absolute value on overlap and no additional dimension factor.

definition_reconstruction.stdGaussian: Pushforward of the finite product of gaussianReal 0 1 through sum_k z_k e_k for the supplied orthonormal basis.
definition_reconstruction.gaussianReal_variance_convention: The printed density is (sqrt(2*pi*a))^-1 exp(-(t-mu)^2/(2*a)) for positive variance parameter a. The actual target uses mu=0,a=1.
definition_reconstruction.Hermite: Although the raw recursive body is an internal Nat.brecOn implementation, the supplied hermite_zero and hermite_succ equations fully determine H_0=1 and H_(m+1)=XH_m-H_m prime. Thus the normalization is inferred from formulas, not from the name.
definition_reconstruction.aeval: Evaluation Polynomial.eval2 (algebraMap Z R) at the indicated real inner product; integer coefficients use the actual standard integer-to-real algebra map shown in the explicit statement.
definition_reconstruction.G: H_i(<u,x>) multiplied in R by H_j(<v,x>), with the same Gaussian argument x.
definition_reconstruction.conditional_result: An if on equality of natural numbers i,j. If equal, multiply Nat.factorial i cast to R by the ordinary natural power of the real inner product <u,v>; otherwise return real zero.
definition_reconstruction.Integrable: AEStronglyMeasurable plus HasFiniteIntegral with ordinary real norm.
definition_reconstruction.unused_shared_context: Differentiability/fderiv/fderivWithin context is not a new assumption on this polynomial-moment target.

shared_context_verification.method: Exact UTF-8 text equality and SHA256 comparison; common context read once.
